technology_decision: Retain Python exact integer arithmetic for the scalar capture-clock compatibility API: the measured checked Rust/ctypes boundary costs more per call, needs guards plus large-integer fallback, and adds native packaging without an observed benefit for this operation.
scope: P1.3 clock compatibility only. Full clock mapping, calibration, acquisition/decoder/inference and process isolation review remain open; no whole-P1.3 or release qualification.
constraints: Four nonnegative exact integers; reject Boolean, float, nonfinite, missing and string values without coercion or exceptions.
Preserve the inclusive 50000000 ns uncertainty-plus-skew ceiling and exact comparisons beyond binary64/u64 epochs.
Cross-platform offline edge consumer; no external service or new runtime dependency.

research.finding: Integer nanoseconds preserve time precision; selected exact integer arithmetic is consistent with that requirement.
Checked addition and abs_diff provide a credible no-overflow native gate; measured via explicit C ABI, with input guards and fallback required for existing arbitrary-sized integers.
Standard-library FFI supports the no-dependency native comparison; timings include scalar conversion and FFI costs, not just Rust arithmetic.

checks.red: 22 incorrect-acceptance failures and 8 TypeErrors in the malformed-input regression before the fix
checks.lint_format_bandit_yaml: PASS; seeded test-only RNG B311 finding explicitly annotated, no security randomness used
checks.hosted: Updated six installed OS/Python jobs; pinned Rust 1.98.1 comparison on Linux 3.13. Hosted execution pending.

limitations: Diagnostic CPU measurement on a shared Mac, not hard latency or resource qualification.
No RSS/native memory benchmark; fixed-width Rust arithmetic is allocation-free but Python integers and FFI have runtime costs.
No general Rust-versus-Python performance conclusion; this tests one scalar FFI boundary, not a native whole-worker architecture.
CaptureClock.compatible currently has no production call site; this closes its API admission defect, not a claimed active sensor-fusion change.
Full qualification and all retained unrelated failures remain pending.
